content.title: About
content.content: Black-eyed peas are a variety of cowpea distinguished by a black spot on the creamy seed. The canned version is cooked in brine, preserving flavor, texture, and most nutrients, and is ready to eat straight from the jar.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: In the Southern United States black-eyed peas are considered a symbol of good luck, especially on New Year's Day.
They are a staple legume rich in plant protein and often featured in vegetarian dishes.
A traditional Southern dish called “Hoppin’ John” combines black-eyed peas with rice and spices.
Canning extends shelf life to 2–3 years while retaining most of the nutritional value.
Black-eyed peas belong to the legume family, related to beans, peas, and lentils.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: One cup of canned black-eyed peas provides about 13 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Good source of fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron contributes to oxygen transport in the blood, important for vegetarians.

items.title: Provides folate
items.content: Folate supports cell division and is especially vital during pregnancy.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: The beans raise blood sugar slowly, helping with glucose control.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to legumes, including black-eyed peas.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned versions often contain added salt; choose low‑sodium options if you monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Bacterial growth after opening
items.content: Once opened, store the peas in a sealed container in the refrigerator and consume within a few days to prevent spoilage.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add black-eyed peas to salads, soups, stews, rice dishes, or use them as a filling for tacos. They can also be mashed into a spread for vegetarian patties.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep unopened cans in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer peas to an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 4‑5 days.
